To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

partner support in form of verbal encouragement, sensitivity to the nursing mother, assistance in preventing breastfeeding difficulties and helping with household duties can improve breastfeeding practices.
Partners/fathers who support their wives/partners in breastfeeding are more likely to have their wives/partners breastfeed for longer and to exclusively breastfeed for a longer period of time.

partner support in breastfeeding initiation, duration, and exclusivity was associated with verbal encouragement to new mother, sensitivity of the partner/father to the mother's needs, assisting with household and childcare, and helping with breastfeeding problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of partners/fathers on breastfeeding in the community.
the impact of partner support on a mother's decision and ability to breastfeed.
how fathers and other partners can support women to breastfeed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the evidence is insufficient to draw conclusions on whether partners/fathers can improve breastfeeding outcomes in the community, and that more high quality studies are needed to investigate the role of partner/father support in breastfeeding outcomes.
partners/fathers can play a significant positive role in the breastfeeding process of mothers.
the evidence from this review suggests that support from partners/fathers can positively influence the breastfeeding practices of mothers, particularly in the first six months postpartum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the involvement of partners and fathers in breastfeeding programs and interventions is essential for improving breastfeeding practices among women.
the involvement of fathers and partners in breastfeeding programmes can improve breastfeeding practices and outcomes.
partner/father support is important in the breastfeeding process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
partners/fathers should be involved in breastfeeding promotion and support programmes, and their specific role should be identified and targeted.
partner/father support can play a role in a woman's decision to initiate and sustain exclusive breastfeeding.
partners/fathers can play a positive role in supporting breastfeeding mothers.
